subject: Post-demo recon: migration origin mapping, serving lane preference, and next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khatri <samir@novamed.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@novamed.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@gmail>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@gmail>
Date: 2026-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recon: migration origin mapping, serving lane preference, and next steps

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — appreciate you walking us through the latency SLAs and the current inference topology. Quick recap from our side and a couple items we need to finalize sizing and procurement asks.

Summary / decision points we heard today:
- Migration origins: you're running a mix of calls to a competitor-managed LLM API and an internal self-hosted GPU cluster (K8s + Triton).
- Shortlist for serving lane: leaning toward Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, with VPC/private variant as a hard requirement for PHI workloads in certain regions. Hosted API may be ok for low-risk features.
- Procurement/contract: you expect a procurement window in Q3 and will need SOC 2 + DPA details up front.

What we need from you to size and propose options (attached is a simple matrix to fill):
1) Sample traffic profile (tokens/day, peak RPS, 95th/99th latency targets).
2) Breakdown of PHI vs non-PHI traffic and whether PHI must always ride on private VPC/on-prem.
3) A short list of integrations you need (KMS/HSM type, VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink, identity provider).

Attachments: migration_matrix.xlsx (simple worksheet for traffic and network picks).

Next steps (proposed):
- You fill the matrix and return by EOD Fri so we can size Dedicated pools and scope VPC install.
- Schedule a 45-min sizing call next week to validate numbers and network constraints.
- Laura on our side will surface contract constraints (SLA tiers, reserved commitment options).

If this captures things accurately, I'll put calendar options for next Tue/Wed.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Khatri <samir@novamed.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novamed.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@gmail>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@gmail>
Date: 2026-05-03T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recon: migration origin mapping, serving lane preference, and next steps

Marcus — thanks for the summary and for the matrix. Quick answers inline: 

Traffic / origins:
- Tokens/day (avg): ~120M tokens/day across prod and batch pipelines. Peak RPS: ~320 requests/sec during US morning window.
- 60% of traffic currently calls the external provider (competitor API); 40% runs on our in-house cluster (Triton) for latency-sensitive endpoints.

PHI split & compliance:
- Roughly 18% of requests touch PHI data. PHI must be isolated: those endpoints must use an environment where we control keys and network (VPC or on-prem). Hosted is OK only for anonymized/non-PHI workloads.

Integrations / constraints:
- KMS: we use AWS KMS; for on-prem we'd need HSM support via Thales or equivalent.
- Networking: Prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink; we cannot open public egress from PHI paths.

Procurement timeline:
- We'd like a draft commercial term sheet by mid-June to circulate to procurement. Final contract likely Q3.

Attaching a short requirements doc: novamed_requirements.pdf.

Happy to join a sizing call next week — Tue/Wed afternoon PT works.

Samir
Head of Platform, Novamed
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khatri <samir@novamed.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novamed.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@gmail>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@gmail>
Date: 2026-05-04T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recon: migration origin mapping, serving lane preference, and next steps

Appreciate the numbers, Samir — that's exactly what we need. A couple follow-ups and clarifications so we size Dedicated pools correctly: 

1) Token mix: can you split the 120M/day into prompt vs completion tokens if possible (or give an average token-per-request)? If not, an avg tokens/request value will work.
2) Concurrency shape: is the 320 RPS sustained for >10 minutes, or are you seeing spikes of that magnitude for 1–2 minutes? This affects queuing/burst sizing.
3) PHI endpoints: do you need synchronous low-latency (<150ms p95) for PHI, or can those be batched/async?

Our ask: if you can provide a 48-hour sample trace (anonymized) or even aggregated buckets (per-minute TPS and token counts), we can run that through our sizing engine and come back with: 
- Dedicated GPU pool recommendation (instance types + # nodes)
- Cost estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted blended option for non-PHI traffic
- VPC install checklist (network CIDRs, peering, KMS options).

Proposed time for sizing call: Tue 2026-05-11, 2:00–2:45pm PT or Wed 2026-05-12, 11:00–11:45am PT. I can send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Action items for Novamed: fill migration_matrix.xlsx and share the 48-hour aggregate trace (CSV or consolidated CloudWatch export) if possible.

Thanks — I'll also loop Laura to get the contract template and procurement cadence.

Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@gmail>
To: Samir Khatri <samir@novamed.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novamed.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@gmail>
Date: 2026-05-05T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recon: migration origin mapping, serving lane preference, and next steps

Samir / Marcus — quick procurement/contract notes on our side so expectations are aligned: 

- Reserved Dedicated: We offer 12/24/36 month reserved pools with step-down options. Pricing tied to committed vGPU-hours; we can include a 30–60 day transition credit for migration work.
- SOC 2 / DPA: we will attach SOC 2 type II report and our DPA template alongside the commercial term sheet.
- Security evidence: to speed review, please indicate the primary security reviewers at Novamed and any required attestations (encryption in transit at rest, key custody requirements).

For contract flow: once we have the sizing estimate and a proposed commitment, we'll prepare a term sheet (no legal review required to start). If Novamed needs bespoke CLINs for on-prem support, detail those now.

I'll slot legal review timelines into our calendar once you share who will sign from Novamed and their procurement lead's email.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novamed.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@gmail>
Cc: Samir Khatri <samir@novamed.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@gmail>
Date: 2026-05-07T16:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recon: migration origin mapping, serving lane preference, and next steps

Thanks — confirming next steps from our side: 

1) We'll populate migration_matrix.xlsx and return by end-of-day Friday (2026-05-14).
2) We'll extract a 48-hour aggregated trace (per-minute TPS & token buckets) and sanitize it (no PHI in the export). Expect a secure S3 share link.
3) Scheduling: Tue 2026-05-11 2:00–2:45pm PT works for our infra leads — please send calendar invite.
4) Procurement: I'll send contact info for our procurement lead (Emma Park) and our security reviewer (Rajeev Menon) in a follow-up email to speed the SOC 2/DPA exchange.

Also, for the VPC path: we will need a short list of the exact ports and IP ranges your installer uses so we can pre-check firewall policies — Marcus, can you include that in the sizing follow-up?

Related links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/4971). We'll expect the draft term sheet after the sizing.

Appreciate the responsiveness — looking forward to the sizing call.

Alex Chen
VP Platform Engineering, Novamed
